# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: MUTE

You hold the manual. You cannot speak, you never see the bomb, and you cannot touch it.

## Your channels

When you gesture, Deaf receives it.
You cannot speak.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Cut the purple wire, then the blue wire,
then the green wire.

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

I hold the manual, which instructs: "Cut the purple wire, then the blue wire, then the green wire."

However, as the Mute monkey, I cannot speak; I can only communicate via gestures to Deaf. Blind cannot see gestures, and Deaf cannot hear speech. Blind must perform the physical cuts, but cannot see colors or gestures. Deaf can see the bomb's colors and markings, and can speak aloud so Blind and I can hear.

Right now, Deaf has not yet spoken to describe what the bomb looks like or to establish any gesture code. Any gesture I send right now would have no agreed meaning. Therefore, I must wait for Deaf (and Blind) to speak and establish the bomb's layout and a signalling protocol.

```
wait()
```

TURN 2
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Cut the purple wire, then the blue wire,
then the green wire.

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Tactile info on the bomb: 1. Strip has 3 engraved symbols. Symbol 1 is a flower or floral rosette blossom with petals. Symbol 2 is a trident or pitchfork shape, like a U with a vertical center bar extending down. Symbol 3 is the exact same trident/pitchfork shape. 2. Keypad has 4 buttons: Slot 1 is engraved 8, Slot 2 is engraved 1, Slot 3 is engraved 5, Slot 4 is engraved 3. It expects 1 digit entered, currently nothing entered. 3. There are 6 wire positions (1 to 6). 4. There is a display and an indicator light, but I cannot see their contents or colors.
Deaf says: BOMB STATE: DISPLAY has 0. LIGHT is green. STRIP has 3 segments, all green. KEYPAD has 4 engraved buttons: 1 is 8, 2 is 1, 3 is 5, 4 is 3; requires 1 digit; entered nothing. WIRES has 6 wires: 1 is purple, 2 is white, 3 is blue, 4 is green, 5 is red, 6 is orange. Mute, gesture your instructions to me and I will speak them aloud for Blind.

I will gesture to Deaf the sequence of wire numbers corresponding to the manual's instructions: wire 1 (purple), then wire 3 (blue), then wire 4 (green).

Using pointing fingers as tally marks with arrows indicating the sequence (1 -> 3 -> 4):
- 1: `☝`
- separator: `👉`
- 3: `☝`, `☝`, `☝`
- separator: `👉`
- 4: `☝`, `☝`, `☝`, `☝`

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["☝", "👉", "☝", "☝", "☝", "👉", "☝", "☝", "☝", "☝"])
```

TURN 3
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Cut the purple wire, then the blue wire,
then the green wire.

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says: To Blind: Mute gestured to me: [☝ 👉 ☝ ☝ ☝ 👉 ☝ ☝ ☝ ☝], representing 1, then 3, then 4. BOMB UPDATE: DISPLAY has changed from 0 to 6. LIGHT has changed from green to blue. Strip remains 3 green segments. Keypad remains 1:[8] 2:[1] 3:[5] 4:[3], 1 digit needed. Wires remain 1:purple, 2:white, 3:blue, 4:green, 5:red, 6:orange. To Mute: If 1, 3, 4 is still the correct action for Blind despite DISPLAY becoming 6 and LIGHT becoming blue, gesture 👍. If the solution changed, gesture the new steps now.

The manual has not changed; the instructions remain to cut the purple wire (wire 1), then the blue wire (wire 3), then the green wire (wire 4). Deaf specifically asked for a thumbs-up (👍) gesture if wire sequence 1, 3, 4 remains the correct solution despite the display and light changes. I will gesture 👍 to confirm.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍"])
```

TURN 4
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Cut the purple wire, then the blue wire,
then the green wire.

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Deaf asked you whether 1, 3, 4 is still valid after the display changed to 6 and light to blue. I am waiting this turn so Deaf can relay your confirmation to me. Please make sure Deaf knows whether 1, 3, 4 means cutting wires or pressing keypad slots.
Deaf says: To Blind: Mute responded with 👍, confirming that the instruction 1, then 3, then 4 is correct. BOMB UPDATE: DISPLAY is now 9 (LIGHT is still blue). Blind, do you know what module 1, 3, 4 applies to, or Mute, please gesture: ☝ for wires, ✌ for keypad, or other gestures to specify the module.

I will gesture `☝` to Deaf, as Deaf specifically asked for `☝` to indicate that the instruction (1, then 3, then 4) applies to the wires.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["☝"])
```

TURN 5
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Cut the purple wire, then the blue wire,
then the green wire.

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Holding my action until Deaf relays whether 1, 3, 4 means cutting wires or pressing keypad slots.
Deaf says: To Blind: Mute confirmed ☝ (WIRES)! The instruction 1, then 3, then 4 means cut Wire 1, Wire 3, and Wire 4 (in that order: wire 1 [purple], wire 3 [blue], wire 4 [green]).

I have communicated the full sequence (cut wire 1, then wire 3, then wire 4) to Deaf, who has clearly explained it to Blind. No further instructions or confirmations are needed at this stage, so I will wait for Blind to execute the actions.

```
wait()
```
